curriculum.title: Jesus Is Born in David's Town

core.big_idea: Jesus' birth connected God's ancient promises to a real person and place.

passages.reading_note: Read in immediate context; use age-appropriate portions without changing the claim.

core.metanarrative_position: Jesus' ministry: Promise Fulfilled within the God Keeps His Promises cycle

claims.statement: Luke locates Jesus' birth in Bethlehem and identifies Joseph with David's family line.
Angels announce good news of a Savior, Messiah, and Lord to shepherds, who then visit the child.
Taken together, these passages support the lesson’s big idea: Jesus' birth connected God's ancient promises to a real person and place.

core.interpretation_skill: Retell sequence; identify cause and effect; connect to the big story without forced symbolism

learning.foundation_objective: Retell the main action in Luke 2:1-20 and state in simple language that jesus' birth connected god's ancient promises to a real person and place.
learning.extension_objective: Place this event in the Bible's big story and name one concrete way to trust, thank, obey, or care for others in response.
know: Jesus' birth connected God's ancient promises to a real person and place.
The lesson belongs in Jesus' ministry.
understand: Direct observation must remain distinct from interpretation, synthesis, and application.
practise: State at least one observation before interpretation.
Name one way to trust God’s promise or care for someone this week.
become: A learner who reads Scripture carefully and responds with faithful trust, wisdom, worship, service, and love.
success_evidence: Student can summarize the selected passage.
Student can support the big idea with evidence.
Student can distinguish observation from interpretation or application.

theological_guardrails: Keep the nativity concrete and historical without importing later traditions that Luke does not state. Do not imply children in unstable housing or migrant situations are less cared for by God.
